Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexlify Q2 FY25 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Nexlify's Q2 FY25 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Thompson, CFO; Dr. Lena Novak, CTO; Jordan Lee, Chief Revenue Officer; Emma Patel, Chief Product Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Marketing Officer; and Taylor Kim, Chief Customer Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Nexlify's performance for Q2 FY25. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our FlowAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on eight key areas: capital allocation, customer mix, product roadmap, cash runway, LTV/CAC ratio, free cash flow, average contract value or ACV, and expansion revenue.

These areas highlight our disciplined approach to growth and profitability in the AI-native SaaS landscape. On the product front, our innovations are gaining traction, and financially, we're generating robust cash flows while optimizing our customer base. Mike will dive deeper into most of these shortly, but first, a quick note on our momentum—we're executing against our Rule of 40 targets with confidence.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $312 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $81 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $1.25 billion to $1.30 billion.

Turning to our capital allocation strategy, which remains a cornerstone of our disciplined approach to driving long-term shareholder value. We've generated robust free cash flow—$528 million over the trailing twelve months, up 32% year-over-year—bolstered by our Rule of 40 score of 48, with ARR growth at 28% and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 37%. With $1.4 billion in cash and equivalents and minimal net debt, we have significant dry powder to execute flexibly across our four-pillar framework: organic R&D reinvestment, tuck-in acquisitions, capital returns, and opportunistic balance sheet optimization.

Organic investments command the lion's share—about 45% of our TTM FCF, or $238 million. We're doubling down on R&D to lead in AI-native workflow automation, allocating $150 million this year to GenAI initiatives like FlowAI, now powering 65% of customer workflows with agentic AI for autonomous task orchestration and no-code integrations tailored for mid-market enterprises. Another $60 million goes to zero-trust security enhancements amid a 42% YoY rise in ransomware attacks, exceeding SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 standards. Regionally, 25% targets APAC expansion, with FlowAI localized for Mandarin and Japanese, fueling 55% ARR growth there against IDC's 22% market forecast.

M&A takes about 25% of FCF, or $132 million deployed YTD, from a pipeline over $800 million. We're targeting bolt-ons to expand our TAM and tech moat, like our $85 million acquisition of StreamForge for real-time collaboration APIs now boosting Nexlify Teams and net retention to 118% in media and consulting. In EMEA, the $47 million DataWeave deal adds ML analytics for Europe's 31% CAGR composable SaaS market. We focus on $50-150 million deals at >10x ARR multiples for 20-30% FCF accretion within 18 months.

Capital returns to shareholders are 20% of FCF, or $106 million, with $72 million repurchased YTD at $145 average, retiring 1.2% of float at our 15x forward EV/FCF versus the SaaS index at 18x. No dividends yet as we're growth-focused, but reassessing at 40% margins after five years of 35% EPS CAGR.

Balance sheet fortification is 10% opportunistic, including $50 million debt prepays at 4.2% yields and $20 million in 5.2% high-yield money markets. We expect $650-700 million FCF in FY25, holding this mix while scaling M&A if valuations ease.

Next, our customer mix continues shifting decisively toward enterprise, now driving 75% of our $1.2 billion total ARR, up from 68% YoY and 62% two years ago. This stems from GTM execution, land-and-expand, and digital transformation tailwinds. SMBs are 25% of ARR but 65% of our 32,000 customers.

In Q2, enterprise customers hit 1,850, up 28% YoY and 8% QoQ, contributing $900 million ARR at $285,000 average ACV—a 12% YoY rise from multi-year deals. NRR here is 128%, with 25-30% cohort expansions via AI Decision Engine and Forge Analytics Pro.

SMBs reached 30,150 customers, up 22% YoY, with $300 million ARR at $18,500 ACV and 112% NRR, though churn rose slightly to 8% annualized from pruning low-engagement accounts. Enterprise net adds grew 45% YoY to 320, like our GlobalBank expansion from $150k to $2.5M ARR.

SMB growth slowed to 18% amid budgets, but freemium conversions hit 32%. Enterprise Guardrails with FedRAMP and ISO certs won regulated sectors; SMB AI Workflow Builder cuts time-to-value to 10 minutes.

Regionally: North America (65% ARR) enterprise at 82%; EMEA (20%) 70/30 with 30% SMB surge; APAC (15%) SMB-heavy at 60%, ramping enterprise.

This mix supports Rule of 50, with enterprise at 85% gross margins. We're adding 50 AEs for $1M+ deals, piloting usage pricing for SMB. FY25 enterprise share to 78-80%, with 15% new enterprise from SMB upsells.

On cash position and runway, we ended Q2 with $452 million in cash, equivalents, and short-term investments—up 8% from Q1's $418 million. This reflects $68 million operating cash flow from $312 million revenue and 52 DSO, plus $42 million FCF with 4% capex.

Adjusted burn was $28 million, down 15% YoY, from R&D in AI Agent (25% NRU uplift) and headcount optimization to 1,450 employees. This gives a 24-month runway conservatively, extending to 30+ months with Q3 growth to $325-330 million and $1.35 billion FY25 ARR.

North America is 72% inflows at 95% margins; EMEA 45% ARR growth to $180 million; APAC 82% margins. We're earmarking $150 million for AI R&D, $75 million tuck-in M&A, $100 million buybacks at $42 average.

Our LTV/CAC ratio expanded to 4.2x in Q2, up from 3.8x last quarter and 3.4x YoY—sixth straight expansion, matching Snowflake and HubSpot.

LTV: ARPU $148k enterprise/$42k SMB, 82% margins, 52-month lifetime at 118% NRR and 0.19% monthly churn via AI prediction—blended LTV $312k.

CAC: $78M S&M (28% revenue) / 1,320 new customers ($148k ACV) = $59k, down 5% QoQ via PLG.

Payback 14 months. North America 4.5x, EMEA 3.9x, APAC 3.4x. Drivers: 55% freemium (1.3x viral), AI 25% NRR lift, 28% partner revenue. Expect 4.5x year-end.

Free cash flow was $48 million in Q2, up 28% YoY from $37.5 million, sequential from $42 million—11th straight positive quarter, TTM margin 22% up from 18%. FY24 tracking $185 million at 21%.

Operating cash $52 million from 118% NRR, $462 million ARR +28%, $720 million RPO +45%. DSO 54 days, multi-year 35% new ACVs.

Margins up 420bps to 26%, S&M 32% (CAC $8,200 enterprise, -12%), R&D 22%. Capex 1.2%. North America 68%, EMEA +40%, APAC 12%.

Expect 25%+ margins FY26 via 115%+ NRR, 28% S&M. $620 million cash deploys to AI, M&A, repurchases.

ACV hit $52,300 in Q2, +22% YoY from $42,800, +8% QoQ—record high, TTM $49,200 +19%.

Enterprise $168,000 +28%, from $5.2M deals. Mid-market $42,500 +15% via 35% cross-sell. SMB $12,800 +5%.

North America $55,400 +25% (62% bookings), EMEA $48,900 +19%, APAC $46,200 +31%, LatAm $38,500 +12%.

Drivers: AI Suite 42% expansion, 85% attach; ValueRealization Teams 68% win rates; consumption pricing. Guide Q3 $54-56k, FY $51,500 +18%, FY26 $60k+.

Expansion revenue reached $28.4 million, +42% YoY, 12% QoQ—32% of $89.2 million revenue, net $22 million to $412 million ARR. Top 20% drove 62%, mid 38%, SMB 25%.

Median land-to-expand 9 months; usage 18% ($5.1M). Flow launch $4.8M ARR; API/ERP 15%; Marketplace $2.3M.

U.S. 71% +45%, EMEA +55%, APAC +68%. Q3 $30-32M, 116-120% NRR. 92% gross retention.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lena Novak for a technology update.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Emma Patel will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Emma Patel:
Thank you, Lena. We've been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce strong traction from recent launches. Our roadmap prioritizes an AI-first approach, contributing to 28% YoY ARR growth to $478 million and 118% NRR, with new logo ACV up 22% to $156k.

Nexlify AI Copilot, launched Q1 with fine-tuned models on sales data, saw 42% adoption—over 4,200 accounts—lifting productivity 25%, shortening sales cycles 14%, adding $22 million ARR, and cutting churn risk 35%.

Q2 Sales Workflow Automation Suite with no-code builders and intent signals hit 19% enterprise attach, 55% North America adoption, growing EMEA 36% to $92 million ARR.

H2 pillars: AI ubiquity with Q3 Predictive Playbooks (32% win rate beta); composable Marketplace (150+ integrations, 27% QoQ expansions); global scale with Q4 Zero-Trust Edge in APAC, ESG module.

R&D at 18% revenue funds 25+ releases, NPS 68. Positions us for 30%+ ARR FY25.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Emma. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 35% increase in website traffic and a 42% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences and this quarter, we focused on improving our customer support and onboarding processes. As a result, we have seen a 18% increase in customer satisfaction scores.

Mike Thompson:
Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of FlowAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, what's the competitive landscape like, and how do you plan to differentiate yourselves?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Ben. FlowAI has been transformative, powering 65% of workflows and contributing to 28% revenue growth with expansions adding over $22 million in ARR from early adopters. Attach rates are at 42% within 90 days, exceeding our 30% initial expectations by driving 25% productivity gains and 118% NRR.

Competitively, we're ahead of ServiceNow in no-code AI for mid-market, with deeper integrations versus legacy players. Differentiation comes from agentic AI orchestration, zero-trust security, and composable architecture—our marketplace and regional localizations give us an edge in APAC and EMEA, where we've outpaced market growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, what are your expected ROI from these investments, and what are the key challenges you anticipate?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Lisa. International expansion is key, with APAC at 52% YoY growth to $38 million ARR, now 15% of total. Plans include $150 million R&D for localization—Mandarin/Japanese FlowAI, Singapore/Sydney edges—and partnerships like NTT analogs.

Key markets: Japan telcos/e-commerce, India digital transformation, ANZ enterprises. ROI targets 25%+ IRR via 55% ARR growth versus 22% market, with high 82% margins.

Challenges: regulatory like DPDP Act, longer cycles, FX—but offset by FedRAMP pursuit and data sovereignty.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, what's the impact of pricing changes on churn, and what are your long-term targets for NRR?

Mike Thompson:
Thanks, David. Churn is low at 2.3% annualized (0.19% monthly), managed via AI prediction flagging risks 45 days early for 30% renewal boost. NRR steady at 118%, highest ever, with enterprise 128%.

Strategies: proactive expansions, Forge Enterprise Guardrails, viral PLG (1.3x coefficient), white space mapping for 25% attach.

Pricing pilots—hybrid seat/usage—reduced SMB churn from 8%, no contraction impact. Long-term NRR 125%+ by FY26 via AI monetization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays.

Rachel Kim:
Can you provide more color on customer acquisition costs (CAC) and payback periods for new customers?

Mike Thompson:
Sure, Rachel. CAC is $59k per customer, down 5% QoQ from $78M S&M on 1,320 net adds at $148k ACV. PLG drives 55% freemium cohort CAC 40% lower; partners payback <9 months.

Payback compressed to 14 months overall, under 18-month target, with 4.2x LTV/CAC. Enterprise fastest at 12 months.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
